A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same AI-Work/SSA research, with matching authors, market framework and retained experiments despite the changed title. Text, equations, figures, tables and all appendices are readable and support comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original market simulations, LLM comparisons, SSA prompting experiments, capability ablations and trace–reward analyses in Sections 4–5 and the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds prompt-control experiments, mechanism robustness tests, scalability results and quantitative human validation of trace scoring.

M1.justification: The SSA reasoning scaffold and bid/train market loop remain. v2 extends the specified framework with interactive cipher/ordering execution using persistent task memory and hint-based learning (Appendix B.5). Contract-specific shared instructions also replace v1's differing payment instructions for SSA and its baselines. These changes are localized extensions and corrections.

E1.justification: v1 evaluates proxy-task markets. v2 describes CipherTask and OrderingTask and mentions interactive execution, but provides no clearly identifiable experimental configurations or results for those tasks. Its population-size and mechanism sweeps otherwise retain proxy-market tasks. Whether evaluated task coverage actually expanded is therefore uncertain.

E2.justification: Beyond the retained CoT, ReAct and policy baselines, v2 evaluates structure-only SSA, knowledge-only SSA and four alternative reasoning scaffolds (Tables 18–19). Fixed/FIXPL corresponds to Specialist/SPEC, rather than an entirely new comparator, although its documented policy changes. Greedy also changes from no voluntary training to probabilistic training.

E3.justification: Reported baseline settings change from reputation window 10, forgetting factor 0.85, Gumbel temperature 0 and LLM temperature 0.5 to 5, 0.5, 0.01 and 0.2 where supported (v1 Appendix G; v2 Appendix C). Trace evaluation switches from GPT-5 to Claude-Sonnet-4 and introduces anonymization and quantitative human validation. New prompt controls and scalability studies add evaluation designs. These reporting changes do not establish that retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v1 already contains price-sensitivity, demand-shift, recession and component-ablation analyses. v2 adds tests separating reasoning structure from domain knowledge, alternative scaffold controls, robustness across scoring/reputation/learning/matching mechanisms, and scalability analyses up to 128 agents (Appendices D.3, D.6–D.7). The existing component ablation is also substantively revised.

E5.justification: v2 adds run-level bootstrap 95% confidence intervals, repeated judge sampling, quantified human agreement, model-adjusted reward associations and explicit main-effects ANOVA. Reported repetition counts also change, but remain inconsistent: the SSA summary specifies 25 markets while Table 11 specifies 10 runs; macroeconomic validation specifies 20 runs versus 50 simulations elsewhere. These discrepancies prevent inferring a definite increase in executed runs.

E6.justification: Headline rewards such as SSA's 633.5 and CoT's 419.4 are retained, but v2 adds extensive control, robustness, adaptation and scalability results. The planning ablation changes from little or no benefit in v1 to a positive 0.027 main effect with p < 0.0001 in v2 Table 17. Tables 18–19 add scaffold rankings, and Table 20 reports SSA/CoT reward ratios of 1.22–2.05. v1's token-usage results disappear.

T1.justification: The formal objective changes from infinite-horizon discounted return in v1 Section 3.1 and Appendix E.5 to finite-horizon undiscounted cumulative reward in v2 Appendix B.3.7. This revises the stated horizon and discount assumptions, although both versions primarily evaluate fixed-length episodes. The underlying CES and Bayesian reputation framework remains, without new theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: v1's abstract and introduction claim a first unified framework capturing adverse selection, moral hazard and reputation. v2 narrows the headline contribution to a controlled AI-only market testbed emphasizing adverse selection, reputation and skill-investment tradeoffs. This changes the claimed economic scope, beyond wording alone. A broad novelty assertion nevertheless remains in v2 Appendix A.2.

C2.justification: v2 treats macroeconomic relationships as directional sanity checks rather than sufficient market fidelity and explicitly rejects quantitative forecasting. It qualifies training responses as mechanism-dependent, distinguishes observational trace associations from causal evidence, and interprets prompt-control results as supporting the specific reasoning decomposition. The earlier explanation that planning adds little is removed, and applicability and manipulation risks receive substantive discussion.

D1.justification: v2 supplies substantially fuller implementation information: matching and reputation pseudocode, job-generation distributions, skill initialization and noise, benchmark-feedback mechanics, observation/action examples, control prompts and configuration tables (Appendices B–C). It clarifies that the prompted termination hazard does not terminate simulations. However, v1's detailed metric formulas and token-accounting explanation are not retained.

R1.justification: v2 substantially expands positioning around metacognition/calibration, opponent modeling, planning, LLM economic actors and emerging agent marketplaces (Appendices A.1 and A.4). New connections include human-capital theory, Bayesian games and agent-economy infrastructure. The introduction also shifts from broad first-framework claims toward a more specifically situated economic testbed.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction and substantial portions of the methods and experimental narrative are rewritten. Economic-forces discussion moves into the appendix, and the former separate appendices are reorganized into background, implementation, experiments and results, with a contents page. The main narrative now explicitly separates diagnostic associations, prompting interventions and controlled explanations.

P2.justification: v2 adopts a two-column main layout, resizes and relocates retained figures, and moves trace examples and the ablation display into the appendix. Figure 8 replaces contribution boxplots with present/absent bars. Performance tables are rebuilt into economic and behavioral panels, and substantial configuration, robustness, control and scalability tables are added.

improvement.justification: v2 addresses important evidential gaps through targeted prompt controls (Tables 18–19), mechanism robustness tests (Tables 12–13) and human validation of trace scoring (Appendix C.5). Fuller implementation documentation and narrower simulation claims also improve interpretability. Conflicting SSA run counts and prompt-control horizons—100 rounds in Appendix D.6 versus 50 in Table 18—remain material reproducibility flaws. Nevertheless, the added controlled evidence substantially strengthens support for the paper's central conclusions.
